Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thompson, Chief Operating Officer; and Lisa Chen, VP of Exploration.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production volumes averaging 450,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 8% year-over-year. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on lifting cost reductions, which hit our lowest levels in years through targeted efficiency programs. We are focused on prudent capital allocation, balancing shareholder returns via dividends and buybacks with high-return reinvestments. Further, we are advancing our exploration efforts with promising well results across key basins. Finally, we are taking steps to strengthen our balance sheet, meaningfully lowering debt while maintaining liquidity for growth opportunities.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Patel to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Patel: Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.8 billion, up 20% year-over-year. Operating income was $950 million, and net income was $720 million. We generated $1.1 billion in free cash flow and returned $650 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $14.8 billion in total debt and $2.5 billion in cash and equivalents.

Let me dive deeper into one of our key operational metrics: lifting costs per BOE, which capture our lease operating expenses divided by total production. This gauge of efficiency in lifting hydrocarbons from our assets is crucial, particularly with WTI around $82 per barrel and Henry Hub natural gas near $2.40 per MMBtu. Despite ramping production 8% to 450,000 BOE per day, we've maintained rigorous cost control.

For trend analysis, Q3 2024 lifting costs averaged $9.85 per BOE company-wide, down 12% from $11.20 in Q3 2023 and 5% from $10.35 in Q2 2024. This continues a string of five straight quarters of declines, reaching our lowest since 2019 pre-pandemic. Over five years, we've cut costs nearly 35% from a $15.10 peak in Q2 2020 during COVID disruptions, outperforming peers—Occidental at $10.50 per BOE in Permian last quarter, Chevron's Gulf of Mexico around $12.80. Our half-cycle breakevens stay in the low $40s WTI for solid margin protection.

Regionally, Permian assets—60% of output—led with $7.80 per BOE, a 15% YoY drop from $9.20, via optimizations in Delaware and Midland. Eagle Ford held at $8.50 per BOE, down 4% amid water cut issues in older wells. Gulf of Mexico improved to $14.20 from $16.10 YoY, a 12% reduction from subsea tie-backs at Lobster and Thunder Horse, similar to BP's approaches. North Sea edged to $18.50 due to UK taxes and aging fields, offset by Equinor-style partnerships like Troll revamps.

These gains stem from our 'Efficiency 2.0' program since mid-2022, yielding over $450 million in annual LOE savings. Key drivers include digital transformation with AI predictive maintenance on 85% of 12,000 wells using Halliburton Landmark and our ApexPredict—cutting downtime 22% to 3.3%, Permian rod pump workovers down $1.2 million monthly. Artificial lift shifts, like variable-speed ESPs in 40% Permian wells, trimmed energy use 18%; CO2-lift pilots target another 10%. Water management centralized 25 SWD sites, dropping disposal to $0.62 per barrel, recycling 35% via XRI-inspired tech, saving $25 million in trucking. Supply chain deals with Schlumberger and Baker Hughes locked chemicals 15-20% below peaks, cutting opex 11% YoY. Labor efficiencies via IoT and drones reduced crews 14%, Eagle Ford electrification saved $0.45 per BOE. Field extensions with acid stims and gels added 5% recovery, prolonging life 18 months.

Ahead, Q4 at $9.40 per BOE, full-year $9.75 average—13% below 2023. Risks like natgas spikes hedged 70%. This boosts FCF by $120 million quarterly, aiding M&A like CrownRock with our sub-$10 Permian edge.

Shifting to debt levels, total gross debt at quarter-end September 30, 2024, was $14.8 billion, down 12% from $16.8 billion YE2023. Short-term at $1.2 billion repaid via Permian cash flows, where D&C efficiency hit under $7 million per well. Long-term $13.6 billion at 4.8% average coupon—below 6.5% peer norm—maturing 5.2 years average, including $3 billion 2022 notes at 4.125% due 2032, refinanced partly with $1.5 billion 4.75% due 2034 at 125 bps over Treasuries.

Our RBL redetermination boosted borrowing base 10% to $4.2 billion on Eagle Ford and Bakken PDP updates with ceramic proppants lifting IPs 20%, leaving $2.8 billion undrawn.

Net debt at $12.1 billion, down 18% YE2023 and $0.4 billion QoQ, subtracting $2.5 billion cash from $1.1 billion Q3 op cash flow at 90% FCF conversion, plus $0.2 billion securities. Adjusted net debt $11.4 billion. Asset sales like $850 million North Sea to Harbour Energy fueled Delaware buys.

Leverage at Net Debt/LTM EBITDAX 2.3x, improved 40 bps QoQ from 3.1x YE2023, in 2.0-2.5x target, below Occidental's 2.8x, EOG's 1.9x on $5.25 billion LTM EBITDA from 15% margins. Debt to book cap 28% vs. 35% median. U.S. onshore at 1.8x Permian EBITDA, international 3.0x offset by North Sea exit.

Forward, net debt under $11 billion YE2024 via $2 billion divestitures, capex discipline implying 1.9x leverage. Stress-tested to $60 WTI, investment-grade path intact.

On capital allocation, with $4.2 billion FCF before working capital at $82 Brent amid OPEC+ and Middle East tensions, we prioritize dividends, buybacks, reinvestments. Base dividend up 5% to $0.95 quarterly, payable December 15 to November 30 record, full-year $3.80/share, 12% YoY hike, 4.2% yield at 35% payout vs. 40-45% target. Beats Exxon 3.8%, Chevron 4.1%; net debt/EBITDAX 0.8x lowest decade after $2.5 billion paydowns. Sustainable via 10% growth to 2027 at sub-$50 breakevens.

Buybacks: $4.1 billion YTD under $15 billion authorization, $1.2 billion Q3 at $92/share average, accreted $0.18 EPS, cut shares 2.8%. $10.9 billion left, $5-7 billion 2025 if $75+ oil. At 7.2x EV/EBITDA, 15% NAV discount.

Reinvestment at 15% IRR, 2x NPV10/3 years: $18-20 billion 2025 capex flat, 65% upstream 4-6% growth. Permian $7 billion to 850,000 BOE/d, 15,000-foot laterals, 3,500 lb/ft proppant, SIMOPS 120 pads, D&C $650/ft down 12% YoY, 30% efficiency. Gulf Coast LNG aids gas. Guyana $3.5 billion Yellowtail/Uaru FPSOs H2 2025/2026, 18-month payback $65 Brent, Exxon/Hess partner. Midstream/new energies $2 billion: Dominion JV to 1.5 MMBO/d Permian, Texas CCUS 5 MMtpa CO2 from Freeport LNG for 45Q, blue H2 with Chevron/Air Products. North America 75%, international 20% Brazil Mero/Norway Sverdrup. Avoid low-price shale gas.

Framework: 40% FCF dividends, 30-40% buybacks, 30-40% reinvest; $12.5 billion returned YTD vs. $14 billion capex, 120% FCF yield. Low-cost 3.5-year Tier 1, 7 kg CO2e/BOE.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Thompson for an operational update.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 450,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought several key pads online, including our Northern Delaware development in Lea County, New Mexico, contributing to growth. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives across all regions.

Now I will turn it over to Lisa Chen for an update on our exploration activities.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. Our portfolio spans high-return Tier 1 acreage in Permian Basin, Eagle Ford Shale, and Gulf of Mexico deepwater. We've driven down drill-and-complete costs while boosting productivity via advanced completions and analytics.

In Permian—65% of D&C capex, 70% inventory—we spudded 18 gross wells in Delaware/Midland, online 15 at 98% success targeting Wolfcamp A/C, Bone Spring with 12,000-15,000-foot laterals. Northern Delaware Lea County pad (100% WI, 45,000 net acres) averaged IP30 1,250 boe/d, 72% oil, 12% type curve beat via 60 stages, 2,500 lb/ft proppant, diverters; EUR 950 Mboe, breakeven <$35 WTI. Midland Central Basin Platform three-well pad IP30 1,100 boe/d 68% oil, EUR 850 Mboe; drilling 18 days spud-to-release, D&C $750/lateral ft down 22% QoQ with Patterson-UTI SuperSpec, 85% recycled frac water cutting fresh 40%.

Eagle Ford—20% capex, 120,000 net acres 95% HBP—eight wells Dimmit/La Salle Lower Eagle Ford/Austin Chalk, IP30 1,800 boe/d 85% gas rich NGLs >120 btu, $4.50/MMBtu realized, EUR 1.2 Bcfe, <$4.50/Mcf half-cycle. La Salle pad hybrid channel frac Liberty Energy, 24-hour IP 2,500 boe/d, 30% longer flow; replicate 250+ locations, 12-year inventory.

Gulf of Mexico: Drilled Albatross-1 Green Canyon 450 (100% WI, 15,000 acres Lease Sale 261), 180 ft net oil pay Miocene sands >22% porosity <25% Sw, Netherland Sewell 450 MMboe gross mean 65% success; Q4 completions, H2 2026 first oil Winterfell FPSO tie-back like Chevron Anchor. De-risks 10-well inventory, farm-down Pelican supermajor; $120 million 2025 capex, 3x upside $50 Brent breakeven.

Rig count four operated (three Permian, one Eagle Ford flex), 52 gross completions YTD 10% ahead; flat time down 25% AI torque-drag digital twin Halliburton. 1.2 million acres seismic FWI upgraded 15% unrisked, +200 Mboe PUDs. 90% electric ProFrac fleets cut Scope 1 35% YoY, <0.2% methane, zero freshwater Permian pilots.

H2: 60 gross completions—25 Permian, 12 Eagle Ford, Albatross. $1.2-1.3 billion D&C capex 75% Permian, 15-20% FCF yield $80 WTI/$4 HH. Q1 2025 fifth rig 20,000-ft Waha laterals, Oxy CO2 EOR pilots. 15-year inventory 1,800+ locations $42/boe average breakeven; $75-85 WTI prioritize returns, bolt-on M&A sub-$10k/acre Permian. DD&A $12/boe peer-beating. Q2 adds 12,000 boe/d, year-end 95-100 Mboe/d.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Miller with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Brian Miller: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the lifting cost trends and initiatives?

Alex Rivera: Good morning, Brian. As Sarah outlined comprehensively, our lifting costs have improved dramatically through Efficiency 2.0, with Permian leading at $7.80 per BOE and multiple levers like AI maintenance and water recycling delivering $450 million savings. This gives us a clear competitive edge.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Laura Jenkins: Good morning. What are your expectations for capital allocation and debt reduction going forward?

Sarah Patel: Good morning, Laura. We're sticking to dividends first with the recent hike, aggressive buybacks under the authorization, and reinvestment only in >15% IRR projects like Permian expansions. Net debt trajectory to below $11 billion YE2024 supports this fully.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly: Could you please provide more color on the new wells and drilling efficiencies?

Mike Thompson: Thanks, Tom. Lisa covered the standout results like the Northern Delaware pad's 1,250 boe/d IP30 and Eagle Ford hybrids. Our rig efficiencies and water recycling are key to sustaining these gains into next year.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Smith with XYZ Capital. Please go ahead.

John Smith: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy, particularly regarding development plans and resource potential?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, John. The exploration successes like Albatross-1 strongly bolster our long-term strategy by adding high-impact resources to de-risk inventory.

Alex Rivera: Thanks, John. Great question on our future development plans and resource potential—it's the heart of our value creation story here at Apex Energy Corp. I'll walk you through this in detail, starting with our inventory, then layering in our multi-year development roadmap, technical advancements, and regional breakdowns. Sarah will chime in on the capex tie-in later.

First, let's set the stage with our resource base. As of YE2023, proved developed producing reserves—or PDP—stand at 1.2 billion BOE, total proved at 2.8 BBOE. Real upside in 2P 5.1 BBOE and 3P 8.7 BBOE, up 15% YoY from reservoir work. Ryder Scott audits confirm, NPV10 after-tax on 2P >$45 billion at $65 WTI flat—multi-decade runway.

Drilling inventory Tier 1, >7 years at pace: 4,500+ gross locations <$35/bbl breakeven, half <9 months payback strip. Ahead of EOG/Pioneer; industry D&C down 20% since 2021 efficiencies.

Permian crown jewel, 450,000 net acres Midland/Delaware: 3,200 undrilled, EUR 1.2 MBOE 12,000-ft laterals. Q4 Wolfcamp AXL pad eight wells IP30 2,800 BOE/d 75% oil, 45% NTM EUR uplift prop curve. Ramp 10 rigs 2024, 25% YoY growth 350,000 BOE/d cash flow funded. EOR CO2 pilots Midland capture nano-foam 25% sweep, 15-20% recovery, 500 MMBOE 2P by 2026 like Oxy.

Eagle Ford 180,000 net Karnes/DeWitt: 1,100 locations oil/condensate, 40-stage 3,500 lb/ft fracs IP 1,800 BOE/d up 30%, 18% growth 2024 120,000 BOE/d $28/bbl breakeven. Hybrid stacking Austin Chalk/S2, 200 MMBOE stacked; Halliburton diverters 95% stim efficiency vs. 80% basin.

Gulf of Mexico: 25% WI Olympus mini-K2 400 MMBOE net 2P 65% oil; Phase 2 three subsea to host Q3 2025 15,000 BOE/d net, $450 million capex >40% IRR $70 Brent. Hadrian North sidetrack 150 ft Wilcox pay; success 1 BBOE contingent, 4D seismic ML on Chevron Anchor.

Exploration 10% $2.8 billion 2024 capex $280 million: Guyana 12.5% Block Z carried Exxon/Hess two 2025 prospects 500 MMBOE gross Liza-style. Bakken 120,000 acres McKenzie 800 locations Three Forks 900 MBOE EUR, 15,000-ft laterals 10% uplift, Emerson digital twin NPT cut 40%.

ApexNext $150 million: AI seismic NVIDIA 10,000 sq mi Permian +15% Tier 1. Completions 2,500 psi SLB fluids 10% less water cut. All-electric Eagle Ford 80% GHG cut, SEC/IRA ready. CCUS 5 MMTPA 2030 45Q Occidental hubs.

Returns discipline: $82 Brent OPEC+/Asian LNG 2.5x FCF ROIC strip, capex eff down 12% YoY BOE, 50% FCF returns buybacks/dividend. Organic first, $1.2B Delaware bolt-on. Risks Red Sea/EV hedged $40 floor 65% fixed gas; $60 drill 80% profitable. 15-20% CAGR prod 2028, 2P to 7 BBOE 20%+ IRR.

Sarah Patel: Thanks, Alex. Our $2.8B program is back half-loaded: Q1-Q2 $650M quarterly, H2 $900M rigs up. 70% D&C, 15% facilities/infra, balance exploration/base. Funded in $4.5-5B EBITDA, $2.2B FCF target.

Alex Rivera: John, does that cover it, or questions on specifics?

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
